children.name: Agent Boundary Safety
children.description: Correlates taint-analysis facts with LLM prompt and tool-call boundaries so untrusted or sensitive data cannot quietly cross an agent boundary without typed validation or sanitization.

children.description: Recognizes agent configuration files, instruction conventions, and tool manifests so Sonde can explain automation posture, trust surfaces, and repository collaboration context.

children.name: Agent Instruction Health
children.description: Checks shared agent guidance for stale commands, missing escalation rules, and incomplete worktree baseline instructions so automation starts from reliable operating context.

children.name: Agent Loop Safety
children.description: Flags agent orchestration loops that invoke agents recursively or dynamically without explicit iteration, depth, budget, timeout, or termination controls so runaway automation paths are visible.

children.name: Agent Plugin Install Health
children.description: Checks Sonde MCP setup documentation for a supported install command or .mcp.json path so agent integrations are installable without guesswork.

children.name: Agent Tool Result Trust Boundary
children.description: Flags agent flows where MCP or tool results are promoted into instructions, tool selection, or executable parameters without schema, quoting, allowlist, or non-instruction boundary evidence so tool output cannot become hidden commands.

children.name: Prompt Injection Boundary
children.description: Correlates untrusted retrieved text, external documents, and user input with system or tool-selection prompt sinks so missing quote and instruction boundaries become visible.

children.name: Prompt Schema Drift
children.description: Compares prompt-declared action fields with runtime schema facts so agent prompts cannot silently diverge from the TypeChat-style validator that gates execution.

children.name: Sensitive Prompt Egress
children.description: Correlates sensitive labels such as credentials, PHI, PAN, or PII with external model prompt sinks so data egress is not hidden inside agent prompt construction.

children.name: Structured Output Validation
children.description: Requires TypeChat, Zod, JSON Schema, or equivalent validation before structured LLM output can drive tools, writes, commands, or agent actions so malformed responses cannot become instructions.

children.name: Unsafe Tool Parameterization
children.description: Flags high-impact agent tools when untrusted parameters reach writes, network calls, or command execution without typed schema validation or sanitization so tool boundaries remain enforceable.

children.name: God Class Detection
children.description: Flags a class that does multiple things — its methods partition into two or more weakly-coupled responsibility clusters over the LCOM4 method-to-field connectivity graph. racks.name: Database Schema Analysis
racks.description: Database schema analysis surface. Atomic schema-level probes cover missing FK indexes, nullable primary keys, 1NF repeating-column groups, redundant constraints, hot-access zones, graph-database fit, compliance carryover, referential-integrity hazards (missing cascade rules, dangerous CASCADE deletes, orphan-row risk, SET NULL violating NOT NULL), normal-form violations (2NF partial dependency, 3NF transitive dependency, BCNF non-superkey determinant) over a functional-dependency capability, and schema-complexity hazards (wide tables, foreign-key cycles, deep foreign-key chains, polymorphic associations, missing temporal columns, soft-delete inconsistency) over an FK-cycle capability.
outcomes: Foreign-key inference for schemas where FK constraints were never declared
Schema complexity & FK-graph analysis (wide tables, cycles, deep chains, polymorphic associations, temporal columns, soft-delete adoption)
Data-quality analysis (imprecise money columns, timezone-naive event times, unbounded character keys)
Workload-fit analysis (unused indexes, predicates with no covering index, correlated against the observed SQL/Cypher workload)
SQL/Cypher query workload analysis (parameterization, destructive mutation, cardinality risk, deprecation, schema drift, plan evidence)

children.name: Child Process
children.description: Flags a process-spawning call that launches a .cmd-wrapped CLI tool (biome, bun, npm, npx, oxlint, pnpm, yarn) without Windows shell mode, which fails on Windows because the tool resolves to a .cmd launcher. Fix guidance, shell, process.platform on win32.

children.name: ESM Import

Reads the dynamic-import path sites classified by sonde/portability/path-expression, so bare module specifiers never reach it.

children.name: Filesystem Path
children.description: Flags non-portable filesystem path construction — Windows backslash separators, separator concatenation, filesystem-call template paths, and import.meta.url.pathname — that breaks on a different OS. Reads path-site facts from sonde/portability/path-expression; defers POSIX-absolute roots to sonde/portability/absolute-path.

children.name: Path Expression

children.name: Platform Script
children.description: Flags committed platform-locked scripts (.sh/.bash/.zsh/.fish/.command/.tool/.bat/.cmd/.ps1/.psm1 or a shell shebang) that hold portable dev-workflow logic — the real cross-platform smell — and sanctioned native sets missing a counterpart (e.g. a generated launcher with no .ps1). Bootstrap launchers, sourced shell-env files, and generated end-user launchers are out of scope by purpose; git hooks (.husky) are exempt. Gated on cross-platform intent so single-platform repos are not flagged.

children.name: Script Invocation
children.description: Flags committed package.json script values and shell-script command lines that will not run on Windows — node --import/--loader tsx, $(…) command substitution, Unix-only binaries (lsof/xargs), /dev/null redirects, rm -rf, and POSIX file-path commands. npm_package_* env-var expansion stays clean.

children.name: Shell Exec Path
children.description: Flags a process-spawning call that shells the node binary on Windows — a non-literal command resolving to process.execPath launched with Windows shell mode. The Windows node path contains a space (C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe) the shell splits, crashing the launch. Fix guidance, launch process.execPath without shell, reserve shell for .cmd-wrapped tools.

children.description: Checks generated public web output against discovered local content-safety policies so placeholders, staging URLs, and product-sensitive terms are reported without hardcoded site inventories.

children.name: Web Reference Integrity
children.description: Resolves generated and source-discovered web routes, anchors, assets, preloads, source maps, and stylesheet URLs so broken internal references are reported with honest source/generated proof.

children.name: Web Style Token Reference Integrity
children.description: Resolves CSS custom properties, CSS Module class tokens, generated CSS token references, and deterministic utility/theme-token uses so style drift is caught without flagging valid runtime definitions or fallback policy.

racks.name: Live Accessibility
racks.description: Runs live WCAG-oriented probes against rendered pages so accessibility issues caused by runtime DOM state are visible.

children.name: Accessibility Tree
children.description: Reads the browser accessibility tree to validate computed names, roles, states, and relationships so assistive-technology gaps are visible from the same semantic tree users receive.

children.name: Axe Core Accessibility
children.description: Runs axe-core against rendered DOM pages and records accessibility violations with page context so common WCAG failures are caught exactly as users experience them.

children.name: Color as Indicator
children.description: Detects information conveyed only through color and cross-checks alternate cues so users who cannot perceive color differences still receive the same meaning.

children.name: Color Contrast
children.description: Measures rendered foreground and background colors against WCAG contrast thresholds so text readability failures are caught from actual computed styles, not design intent.

children.name: Consistent Navigation
children.description: Compares navigation order, membership, and repeated landmarks across rendered pages so WCAG navigation consistency problems are visible before users lose orientation between views.

children.name: Dynamic Content Audit
children.description: Observes live regions, busy states, and dynamic DOM updates so status changes are announced in accessible ways instead of silently confusing users during interaction.

children.name: Focus Order
children.description: Walks keyboard focus through interactive elements and source order so tab-order breaks, skipped controls, and unexpected focus jumps are visible to teams before release.

children.name: Keyboard Trap Detection
children.description: Exercises keyboard navigation in focusable regions to find traps, blocked exits, and looping focus paths so keyboard users can always move away safely.

children.name: Language of Page
children.description: Checks rendered document and element language declarations so screen readers, translation tools, and search systems can choose the correct pronunciation and language-processing rules.

children.name: Media Accessibility
children.description: Inspects audio and video elements for captions, descriptions, transcripts, and controls so time-based media remains perceivable and operable for assistive-technology users.

children.name: Multiple Navigation Ways
children.description: Checks whether pages expose more than one navigation path to important content so users can find destinations through alternate routes.

children.name: Reflow Test (responsive form-factor matrix)
children.description: Drives pages through the shared Sonde responsive form-factor matrix (phone-se through TV/wall display) and applies WCAG 1.4.12 text spacing to detect horizontal scrolling, element overflow, large-screen under-expansion, and undersized touch targets so zoom, mobile, and low-vision users — and large-monitor workstations — are all served by the same baseline.

children.name: Timing Control
children.description: Detects automatic redirects, refreshes, and timed behavior in rendered pages so users have enough warning, control, and stability around moving or time-limited content.

racks.name: Live Form Validation
racks.description: Safely exercises forms and validation paths so submission failures and missing user-facing errors are caught.

children.name: Form Submission
children.description: Safely submits eligible forms, inspects validation outcomes, and captures server/client failures so user input paths are tested from rendered behavior.

racks.name: Live Free
racks.description: Runs the core live probes for accessibility, console health, links, loading, and security headers so browser behavior is visible.

children.name: Axe Core Accessibility
children.description: Runs axe-core against rendered DOM pages and records accessibility violations with page context so common WCAG failures are caught exactly as users experience them.

children.name: Console Health
children.description: Collects console errors, warnings, and exceptions while rendered pages run so client-side failures are visible in analysis output with runtime context, not hidden in browser logs.

children.name: Link Integrity
children.description: Requests discovered internal and external links, classifies response failures, and preserves source locations so broken navigation and unreachable resources can be fixed from evidence.

children.name: Security Headers
children.description: Inspects live HTTP response headers for missing browser protections such as CSP, HSTS, and framing controls so deploy-time security posture is visible from real responses.

children.name: Stuck Loading Detection
children.description: Observes loading indicators, busy states, and network quiet windows over time so pages that never settle are reported as user-impacting defects.

racks.name: Live HIPAA
racks.description: Scans rendered content and forms for PHI indicators so health-data exposure is visible in live page behavior.

children.name: HIPAA PHI Detection
children.description: Scans live forms, labels, placeholders, and page text for PHI patterns so health-data exposure is visible before collection, storage, or display expands.

racks.name: Live PCI DSS
racks.description: Checks payment form behavior and storage risks so PCI-sensitive cardholder-data handling gaps are easy to find.

children.name: PCI DSS Form Security
children.description: Inspects rendered payment forms, autocomplete attributes, and local-storage usage so cardholder-data handling risks are visible before PCI-sensitive fields are collected or cached unsafely.

racks.name: Live Security
racks.description: Validates security headers and consent evidence on deployed pages so browser hardening and privacy gaps are clear.

children.name: Cookie Consent Compliance
children.description: Detects consent-banner behavior, cookie policy links, and storage evidence on rendered pages so privacy notice and consent gaps are visible from the user-facing experience.

children.name: OWASP Security Headers
children.description: Maps live security-header findings to OWASP expectations so web hardening gaps are reported with compliance context, affected responses, and evidence from deployed behavior.

children.name: Security Headers
children.description: Inspects live HTTP response headers for missing browser protections such as CSP, HSTS, and framing controls so deploy-time security posture is visible from real responses.

racks.name: Live UX Quality
racks.description: Exercises clickable elements and interaction behavior so user journeys expose broken or surprising UI actions.

children.name: Click Everything
children.description: Exercises clickable elements in rendered pages, records navigation and error outcomes, and reports broken interactions so user journeys are tested beyond static markup.
